thread:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock acceptance criteria for BYOK retention edge cases for next sprint. Customers keep asking about partial key rotations and staggered tenant retention policies. Can we triage?

aj: quick note — staggered retention (tenant-level overrides) is doable but adds complexity to the archival pipeline. We need one of: a) per-tenant retention index, or b) a retention-lambda that evaluates on ingest. b is faster to ship.

sam: security POV — if we do per-tenant overrides, we must ensure no cross-tenant leakage in indexing. Also BYOK + tenant-retention + legal hold combos are a nightmare. Need explicit rules for precedence.

lina: legal: precedence should be Legal Hold > Customer Retention > Default Retention. If a legal hold exists, exports and deletions must be blocked even for tenants with short retention. We'll need an audit flag on blocked-deletes.

taylor: CS has two customers on this exact ask: one wants short retention for EU tenants, another wants long retention + key rotation windows. Both require clear SLA wording. Can we get decision this week?

maya: Proposal: ship minimal UX + safe server-side rules: - retention override per-tenant (opt-in) implemented as \"retention_window_ms\" on tenant metadata - legal hold always blocks deletion and shows audit reason - key rotation: support staged rotations where old key decrypts archived blobs for X days (configurable)

aj: implementation notes: plan to add a retention evaluation step in ingest pipeline. Pseudocode:```python
# retention check
retention = tenant.metadata.get('retention_window_ms') or org.default_retention
if legal_hold.exists(tenant):
    mark_non_deletable(blob, reason='legal_hold')
else:
    set_expiry(blob, now + retention)
```

sam: Also need KMS policy change: during staged rotations, old-key decrypt must be allowed for archival-service IAM principal. Add to checklist.

lina: Legal wants an exportable event record: for any deletion-block or retention-lift event, record user, timestamp, policy-id. That must be available via audit export API.

maya: Risks: - complexity bump for ingest throughput - potential storage cost spike if many tenants pick long retention - edge-case: what if a tenant has BYOK and key rotation is requested mid-retention? we should document fallback.

aj: For throughput: we'll add a small async queue for expiry-setting so synchronous ingest latency stays the same. Need +1 infra ticket.

ops-bot: New ticket created: INFRA-4291 \"expiry-async-queue for per-tenant retention\" — https://issues.redwood.ai/INFRA-4291 :information_source:

maya: Decision items for sprint: 1) ship per-tenant opt-in retention (server-only) 2) legal hold precedence enforced 3) staged key rotation support (30-day overlap default) 4) audit export fields to include policy-id and block-reason. Approvals?

sam: +1 from security. Need KMS policy doc link in the PR.

lina: +1 from legal on precedence and audit fields. Please include retention-policy table in the export.

aj: +1 from eng, will scope as M, estimate 3 sprints without parallelization, but can MVP in 1 sprint if we cut UI and make it config-only.

taylor: +1 from CS if we get clear release notes and example tenant configs. I can draft a customer-facing FAQ.

maya: OK — ship config-only MVP in sprint. Action items: aj to draft implementation RFC, sam to write KMS policy checklist, lina to specify audit export schema, taylor to draft FAQ. I'll consolidate into a short PRD.

aj: I'll drop RFC by EOD tomorrow.

sam: I'll add KMS checklist items in the RFC comments.

lina: I'll share audit schema doc in this thread by lunchtime.

taylor: I'll start the FAQ doc and ping early customers for feedback.

maya: Thanks all — tagging @sam and @aj for next steps :thumbsup: :eyes:
